Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0053", "row_sha256": "f756d1b491d83ac12f6b7cccc5dbcfb7bfa30ccaa15e533a0fa6d4085054309c", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
need a prompt for the north pier library portal audit, not the audit result itself. this is the screen-reader check for staging build 4.8, and the test session was on may 14. keep the request centered on the account-recovery dialog, not the rest of the site. the dialog opens from the “Forgot password?” link on the sign-in page. it has an email field, a “Send link” button, and a close icon in the upper-right corner. there is also a return link beneath the form. the issue people want us to check is the spoken name for that close control.

we used two desktop combinations: windows 11 with firefox 126 and nvda 2024.1, and macos 14.5 with safari 17.5 and voiceover. the session was at 200% browser zoom, and the tester used the keyboard to move through the dialog. this wasn't a mobile check, so don't fold a phone or tablet case into the request. the tester names on the session notes are riley chen and omar; don't make them sound like they both observed the same thing if the notes don't support that. the evidence folder has the session notes and one 42-second recording. we don't have source-code access, and this is a staging-only audit, not a production change request.

there's one condition for the main action. only if both tested combinations report that the close control is announced without a name when keyboard focus reaches it, ask for draft replacement accessible-name wording for that close control. keep any proposed wording to that control; don't ask for a new dialog design or wording for the email field, send button, or return link. don't request code, implementation steps, or a change to the site. this is just wording to consider in the audit record. the test evidence is what decides whether the condition holds, not a guess from the icon or from one platform.

if that condition does not hold, including if only one combination reports the missing spoken name or the evidence doesn't show the same result in both, ask instead for reproduction notes. those notes should say what was observed in each tested combination and point to the relevant session note or recording evidence. don't make the replacement-name wording the fallback; the useful different action is to document how to reproduce and compare the observations. if the evidence is incomplete, describe that plainly rather than treating it as confirmation. we have not settled what either platform announces, so the request should leave the finding open until someone checks the supplied material.

some detail from the people in the room: riley opened the dialog from the sign-in page and tabbed through the controls, then repeated the sequence after closing it and opening it again. omar was checking the recording time stamps against the written notes. the notes say the close icon is at the upper right, but the recording starts after the page is already loaded, so don't ask for a full sign-in journey recording. the session used the same staging account for both combinations. there is no need to include the account address in the audit output. nobody tested whether sending a recovery email works, and that isn't part of this request. we're checking how this one control is identified by the screen reader, not whether the service sends messages.

one line from omar's notes is, “I can get back to the form, but I don't know what that button is.” keep that as an ordinary quote if it is useful context, and don't turn it into a conclusion about both screen readers. the quote was written during the session; we don't know from that line alone which combination it refers to. the prompt should make clear that the names and combinations in the evidence need to be matched carefully. also, the audit coordinator asked that the eventual note distinguish an observed announcement from a proposed accessible name. don't imply that any wording has been approved, installed, or verified after a change.

for the requested work, the output needs to be a compact audit note rather than a general accessibility review. a numbered section is fine if it helps distinguish the two paths, but don't ask the person to produce both paths as if both outcomes were established. use the primary path only when the two-combination condition is met; otherwise use the reproduction-notes path. it should mention staging build 4.8 and the may 14 session so the note can be identified later. keep the scope on the account-recovery dialog's close control, and don't add a score, severity rating, compliance claim, or broader site recommendations; those weren't part of the material collected.

the final output for whoever does this should contain only the requested audit note, with no greeting, preface, or explanation around it. if the fallback applies, the note can identify that the evidence did not establish the same missing-name result in both combinations, but it shouldn't say the control passed or failed overall. if the primary condition applies, it should give wording to consider, not suggest the team already accepted it. the recorded observations and the actual test combination matter more than making the note sound decisive. please organize all of that into a usable prompt, and stop at the prompt rather than writing the audit note.", "output": "Prepare a compact audit note based on the screen-reader check of the North Pier Library portal, staging build 4.8, conducted on May 14. Focus only on the close control in the account-recovery dialog. The dialog opens from the “Forgot password?” link on the sign-in page and contains an email field, a “Send link” button, a close icon in the upper-right corner, and a return link beneath the form.

Use the session notes and the 42-second recording as evidence. The two tested desktop combinations were Windows 11 with Firefox 126 and NVDA 2024.1, and macOS 14.5 with Safari 17.5 and VoiceOver. The tester used the keyboard at 200% browser zoom. The session notes name Riley Chen and Omar; do not attribute an observation to both testers unless the evidence supports that. The same staging account was used in both combinations. The recording begins after the page is loaded. This was not a mobile check, and there is no source-code access. The audit concerns staging, not a production change.

Choose one of these actions based on the evidence:

1. **If both tested combinations report that the close control is announced without a name when keyboard focus reaches it:** Draft replacement accessible-name wording for that control only. Treat the wording as a proposal for the audit record, not as approved, implemented, or verified. Do not provide code or implementation steps, redesign the dialog, or propose wording for the email field, “Send link” button, or return link.

2. **Otherwise:** Write reproduction notes describing what was observed in each tested combination and pointing to the relevant session note or recording evidence. Use this path if only one combination reports a missing spoken name or if the evidence does not show the same result in both. If the evidence is incomplete, describe that plainly. Do not provide replacement-name wording as the fallback, and do not characterize the control as having passed or failed overall.

Riley opened the dialog from the sign-in page, tabbed through its controls, then repeated the sequence after closing and reopening it. Omar compared recording timestamps with the written notes. The notes place the close icon in the upper-right corner, but the recording does not show the full sign-in journey. Do not include the account address. Sending a recovery email was not tested and is outside the scope of this request.

The session notes include Omar’s statement: “I can get back to the form, but I don't know what that button is.” If useful, retain it as an ordinary quote, without treating it as a conclusion about both screen readers. The line alone does not identify which combination it refers to. Match reported observations to the relevant screen-reader and browser combination, and distinguish an observed announcement from proposed accessible-name wording.

Keep the note specific to the account-recovery dialog’s close control. Mention the build and session date so the note can be identified later. Do not add a score, severity rating, compliance claim, or broader site recommendations. Return only the requested audit note, with no greeting, preface, or surrounding explanation. Use the primary path only if its two-combination condition is met; otherwise use the reproduction-notes path. Do not write the audit note now; use this as the prompt for the person who will review the evidence."}]
